newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP plans routine San Manuel copper close.
newsitem.headline: BHP plans routine San Manuel copper close.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Monday it plans to shut its San Manuel, Arizona, copper smelter for routine maintenance sometime in the second half of calendar 1998.
The smelter currently produces about 350,000 tonnes of copper a year, representing about 25 percent of copper output in the United States.
BHP executive general manger of BHP's copper operations, Jim Lewis, told Reuters the shut-down could take as long as 40 days.
"It will be nine years since the the last rebuild when the maintenance work is done, which is a testament to the efficiency of the smelter," Lewis said.
Most smelters face maintenance shutdowns about once every one or two years, Lewis said.
Some building of copper inventories would occur ahead of the shutdown, although the closure would effectively reduce the smelter's output in 1998, Lewis said.
The smelter, acquired as part of BHP's US$2.3 billion acquisition of the Magama Copper Co in 1996, uses 1.2 million tonnes of copper concentrates annually to produce a smelted metal.

The concentrates are put into a flash furnace that smelts the copper to produce copper matte and slag. The material is then transported to one of three copper convertors where silica is added to produce 99 percent pure blister copper.
It was too early to say when in the second half of 1998 the shutdown would occur, Lewis said.
